---
title: "Beneficiary list: household ID cleaning rationale"
output: html_document
---

This report compares completeness and purchase dates between records with and
without an original household ID, then compares the location encoded in that ID
with the official codes matched on district, cell and village names. All tables
are aggregate; the report does not display names, phone numbers or household IDs.

Run from the repository root, keeping the output in Dropbox:

```r
source("PATHS.R")
rmarkdown::render(
  "ASCENT/usage_survey/preload/beneficiary_cleaning_reasoning.rmd",
  output_dir = DATA_ASCENT_PRELOAD,
  intermediates_dir = DATA_ASCENT_PRELOAD,
  clean = FALSE
)
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

repo_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
while (!file.exists(file.path(repo_root, "PATHS.R"))) {
  parent <- dirname(repo_root)
  if (parent == repo_root) stop("Run from within the repository containing PATHS.R.")
  repo_root <- parent
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)
source(file.path(repo_root, "PATHS.R"))

# Preserve valid UTF-8 while converting the legacy bytes in the source files.
repair_text <- function(x) {
  invalid <- !is.na(x) & !validUTF8(x)
  converted <- iconv(x[invalid], from = "windows-1252", to = "UTF-8")
  if (anyNA(converted)) stop("Unable to decode some input text as Windows-1252.")
  x[invalid] <- converted
  x
}
read_input <- function(path) {
  data <- read_csv(path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (nrow(readr::problems(data)) > 0) stop("CSV parsing problems in ", basename(path))
  data |>
    mutate(across(where(is.character), repair_text))
}

beneficiary <- read_input(file.path(DATA_ASCENT_PRELOAD,
                                   "clean-cooking-beneficiaries-list-raw.csv")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    id_status = if_else(is.na(household_id) | str_trim(household_id) == "",
                        "Missing original HHID", "Original HHID present"),
    purchase_date = lubridate::dmy(date_of_purchase_confirmation_in_et, quiet = TRUE)
  )

admin <- read_input(file.path(DROPBOX_EAQIP, "questionnaires", "01-baseline", "vills.csv")) |>
  mutate(n_official = n(), .by = c(district_key, cell_key, village_key))
admin_unique <- admin |>
  filter(n_official == 1) |>
  select(district = district_key, cell = cell_key, village = village_key,
         districtid_key, cellid_key, villageid_key)
admin_ambiguous <- admin |>
  filter(n_official > 1) |>
  distinct(district = district_key, cell = cell_key, village = village_key) |>
  mutate(ambiguous = TRUE)
matched <- beneficiary |>
  left_join(admin_unique, by = c("district", "cell", "village")) |>
  left_join(admin_ambiguous, by = c("district", "cell", "village")) |>
  mutate(admin_match = case_when(
    !is.na(villageid_key) ~ "Unique",
    ambiguous %in% TRUE ~ "Ambiguous",
    .default = "Unmatched"
  ))
```

## Completeness by original HHID status

The denominator for each percentage is the number of records in that HHID-status
group. Missing includes blank or whitespace-only values. Differences describe the
observed list; they do not establish why a value is missing.

```{r completeness}
key_variables <- c("beneficiary_first_name", "beneficiary_last_name", "phone_number",
                   "district", "cell", "village", "product_name",
                   "date_of_purchase_confirmation_in_et", "tier_level",
                   "product_company_supplier", "amount_to_be_paid_by_end_user",
                   "subsidy_amount")
beneficiary |>
  select(id_status, all_of(key_variables)) |>
  pivot_longer(-id_status, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  summarise(records = n(),
            missing = sum(is.na(value) | str_trim(value) == ""),
            missing_pct = round(100 * missing / records, 1),
            .by = c(id_status, variable)) |>
  arrange(variable, id_status) |>
  kable()
```

## Purchase date and product distributions

Dates are parsed as day-month-year. Unreadable dates are reported separately
from missing dates; percentages are within original-HHID groups.

```{r dates}
beneficiary |>
  mutate(purchase_year = case_when(
    is.na(date_of_purchase_confirmation_in_et) |
      str_trim(date_of_purchase_confirmation_in_et) == "" ~ "Missing",
    is.na(purchase_date) ~ "Unreadable",
    .default = as.character(lubridate::year(purchase_date))
  )) |>
  count(id_status, purchase_year, name = "records") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * records / sum(records), 1), .by = id_status) |>
  kable()
```

```{r products}
beneficiary |>
  count(id_status, product_name, tier_level, name = "records") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * records / sum(records), 1), .by = id_status) |>
  arrange(product_name, tier_level, id_status) |>
  kable()
```

## Matching locations to the official village list

The match uses the exact district, cell and village names. Ambiguous means those
names identify more than one official village, because the source has no sector.
Unmatched and ambiguous records cannot be assigned official codes uniquely.

```{r match-status}
matched |>
  count(id_status, admin_match, name = "records") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * records / sum(records), 1), .by = id_status) |>
  kable()
```

## Original HHID versus name-matched codes

For unique matches, the first two, six and eight digits of a 12-digit original
HHID are compared with the official district, cell and village codes,
respectively. Missing or malformed IDs and non-unique name matches are reported
separately rather than counted as agreements or disagreements. Percentages use
all records in the corresponding original-HHID group. The comparable percentage
uses only records with a valid original HHID and a unique name match.

```{r code-comparison}
compare_level <- function(data, official_code, digits) {
  data |>
    mutate(result = case_when(
      id_status == "Missing original HHID" ~ "Missing original HHID",
      !str_detect(household_id, "^[0-9]{12}$") ~ "Malformed original HHID",
      admin_match != "Unique" ~ paste("Location", str_to_lower(admin_match)),
      is.na(.data[[official_code]]) ~ "Missing official code",
      str_sub(household_id, 1, digits) == .data[[official_code]] ~ "Match",
      .default = "Mismatch"
    )) |>
    count(id_status, result, name = "records") |>
    mutate(
      pct = round(100 * records / sum(records), 1),
      comparable_pct = if_else(result %in% c("Match", "Mismatch"),
                               round(100 * records / sum(records[result %in% c("Match", "Mismatch")]), 1),
                               NA_real_),
      .by = id_status
    )
}
```

### District

```{r district-comparison}
kable(compare_level(matched, "districtid_key", 2))
```

### Cell

```{r cell-comparison}
kable(compare_level(matched, "cellid_key", 6))
```

### Village

```{r village-comparison}
kable(compare_level(matched, "villageid_key", 8))
```

## Decision

Retain households regardless of whether the original HHID is missing. For each
uniquely matched location, use the official village code and assign a four-digit
sequence sorted by beneficiary first and last name. Retain the original HHID for
traceability, flag and exclude ambiguous locations, and stop on unmatched names.
Name ties use the source row order. The resulting IDs depend on the input list and
its ordering, so freeze the ID mapping before sampling or fieldwork; regenerating
it after changes can invalidate existing samples and form preloads.
